chose: mass --check exits 0 with '✓ mass ratchet held' and prescribes re-pinning after buildGraph was gutted to return an empty graph — and --update-baseline then pins files|total=0, lines|total=0, symbols|total=0, undocumented|symbols=0 and silently DROPS lines|app (5 dimensions to 4). Restoring the deriver does not self-heal: --check then exits 1 reporting the project's own pre-existing mass as GROWTH (files|total grew 0->2) and demands a coherence decide justifying mass that was always there.
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

the ratchet has no denominator: 'nothing grew' is computed over the dimensions it happened to read, so a reading that collapsed to zero is indistinguishable from a project that shrank, and the shrinkage prescription actively invites banking the break
discriminatedBy: pin a healthy baseline in a fixture, gut buildGraph, run mass --check and mass --update-baseline, then restore the deriver and run --check again — measured 2026-07-31, all three behaviours confirmed verbatim

because: The instrument was wrong in the way the second candidate named: every one of these ratchets computed its verdict over the dimensions it happened to read and never over the population it read them from, so 0-of-0 and 0-of-500 rendered as the same green. Fixed by giving each ratchet its OWN denominator (mass: graph files+symbols; conventions and lint-sinks: source files scanned, because lintSinks never receives a graph) and a shared rule in floor.ts that refuses a zero reading against a non-empty pin, at --check and --update-baseline alike. Verified by mutation: removing either seam's refusal in any of the three reds the behavioral totality oracle.

chose: an instrument that cannot run throws a typed Unrunnable carrying its report, and cli.ts renders it once for every command
over: a pre-check at each caller of withTreeAt (structuralLog, signal, graphAtRef)
wrapping the whole cli.ts dispatch in try/catch, which would mean restructuring 350 lines of top-level awaits to land an error message
letting the throw stand and documenting the requirement in README
because: A pre-check is a second spelling of the requirement, one per caller, and the third caller added next month is the one that forgets — the drift the command registry exists to end. The typed throw states the requirement ONCE at the seam that discovers it (withTreeAt knows it is git that is missing; the caller only knows it wanted a graph), and the renderer is total over every present and future command by construction. Installed as uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers because every command in cli.ts is a module-level await; anything that is NOT an Unrunnable keeps its stack, because for a genuine harness defect the stack IS the report. Exit 2, the code this CLI already means 'could not run' by (--check with no baseline, unknown verb), never 1 ('ran and failed') and never 0.

chose: each ratchet supplies its own RatchetReading and floor.ts owns the rule; mass reads its remembered denominator off the pins it already carries
over: one shared predicate over the graph, the way cli.ts guards writesArtifacts
adding a denominator field to the baseline file format, which would need a migration and would leave every existing baseline unguarded
because: The three baselined ratchets do not share a vacuity source: mass and conventions take a graph but lintSinks(cfg, mode) never does — it reads scanSources(cfg) — so verify's 'the graph carries no claims' predicate would have guarded one ratchet and silently exempted another, which is the same green-by-absence one level up. Conventions likewise reads its GUARDS from scanSources and takes the graph only to learn which chokepoints are anchored, so an empty graph makes it stricter while an empty SCAN makes it vacuous. No format change was needed for mass because its baseline already records its own denominator: files|total and symbols|total ARE the population, so every baseline ever written already answers the question. For conventions and lint-sinks the pinned COUNT is the lower bound the rule needs — a pinned sink is proof of a file it was found in — and the rule only ever asks the weaker question, was there ever anything here.

chose: writesBaseline is enforced behaviorally from BOTH directions: observed writers must declare it, and declared ratchets must refuse an empty reading at both seams
over: a declared-only flag mirroring writesArtifacts, checked in one direction
a generic guard in cli.ts before the command runs, as writesArtifacts gets
because: A flag checked only against observation proves the registry honest and buys the next ratchet nothing: the day a fourth one is added, the observation oracle passes the moment the flag is set, and the refusal it exists to demand can still be missing. So the second oracle runs every writesBaseline command against a fixture that pins a non-empty baseline in each ratchet's own unit, deletes the code file, and demands a nonzero exit naming [floor] from --check AND from --update-baseline, plus a byte-identical baseline afterwards. Deleting the code file is the honest general collapse: it empties the graph and the source scan at once, so the oracle never has to know which of them a given ratchet reads. A cli.ts guard was rejected for the reason above — there is no one reading it could take that is right for all three. This answers the question left OPEN in commands.test.ts when writesArtifacts landed, and answers it by measurement rather than by taste: the poisoning INVERTS instead of washing out.
